rules.statement: Don't add caller-specific fields (such as what the current caller is permitted to do) to a resource that represents a stored document with its own ETag; expose them from a separate read-only sub-resource that carries no ETag.
rules.why: The document resource is the audit snapshot and its ETag must depend only on the document, while permission answers depend on who asks.
rules.check: Look for permission or caller-derived properties added to a versioned/ETagged resource model, or ETags emitted on responses whose content varies by caller.

rules.statement: Keep authorization decisions on the server and expose the result to the client as a simple flag rather than having the browser compute who holds authority over a node.
rules.why: Computing authority in the browser duplicates the authority chain, including nested hierarchies, and drifts from the server's rules.
rules.check: Look for client or console code that reconstructs the hierarchy or role chain to decide editability instead of reading a server-provided capability flag.

rules.statement: A setting marked as a limit must merge with a meet, and building the descriptor collection must refuse a limit descriptor whose merge is not a meet.
rules.why: Otherwise a scope beneath could override the value set above it, so the limit would only be advice.
rules.check: Look at new setting descriptors with IsLimit set and confirm their merge is a meet; check the collection builder still rejects non-meet limits.

rules.statement: A settings write that adds, removes or changes the JSON value of a limit must require Update permission at the node above the document's node, and fail closed with 403 naming the limits; the node's own administrators cannot raise, lower or remove it.
rules.why: A bound holds only while the scope that wrote it is the only one that can change it, so each limit value has a single author.
rules.check: Look for settings write paths that persist limit changes without checking authority at the parent node, or that compare limits other than by JSON value.

rules.statement: A package marks its own settings that bound lower scopes as limits on the descriptor itself, instead of the host keeping a list of limit names or the descriptor naming a fixed writing tier.
rules.why: The host needs no list, and a fixed tier would tie the setting to tier names and stop a team from limiting its own tenants.
rules.check: Look for new quota or rate-limit settings without the limit flag, or hardcoded lists of limit names in the host.
